Sum all carriers, months, aircraft types, and both directions into each undirected airport pair; retain the giant component.
Inbound/outbound masses count only retained contiguous-US scheduled passenger segments, not international, Alaska/Hawaii, or all-system airport throughput.
Passenger totals are passenger-segments, not unique travelers. Departures are performed departures on the retained positive-passenger rows.
Seats and performed departures exclude zero-passenger rows by the requested filter. They are not total scheduled capacity on all operations.
Static unknown-source objective: a(V)-sum p(C)*a(C). No sequential spread/removal timing or production semantics are changed.
Inbound target weights are exposure/proxy weights at airports, not a count of uniquely protected travelers.
No minimum-traffic threshold is added. Even extremely low-volume CLASS=F routes and their airports remain in the requested network.
Budgets are AT MOST b undirected relationships. Cutting a route suppresses both aggregated directions.
Each row gives one deterministic cardinality-optimal representative, not every co-optimal cut. Its disruption cost need not be minimum among tied protection optima.
BC and BCw are fixed original-graph ordered-pair values; BCw distance=1/passengers. All ties use canonical airport-code order.
BC/passenger divides ordinary unweighted BC by passenger volume; it is a baseline, not the exact cost-efficiency solver.

COMPLETENESS AND EXACT ARITHMETIC
1. Give each original route unit capacity. In a Gomory-Hu tree the minimum tree
edge on an s-t path equals their minimum cut value. Retain tree edges of weight
greater than B. Their components are atoms that cannot be split by <=B removals.
An atom need not induce a connected subgraph; its vertices remain connected in
the surviving ORIGINAL graph under every allowed removal set.
2. Restore cuts internal to each final component. This preserves the objective,
reduces or preserves cardinality and passenger disruption, and leaves exactly
the component boundary. Between two atoms either the entire bundle of original
routes crosses the partition or none does. Bundle cost is its route count.
3. Choose the largest atom as root, and remove it from the quotient graph.
Different remaining branches meet only at that root. In each branch plus root,
enumerate EVERY bundle subset with total cardinality <=B. Deduplicate by its
resulting component partition and restore redundant internal bundles. Every
global feasible partition restricts to one of these local partitions; conversely
every choice of local partitions with total cost <=B gives a feasible partition.
All local root components merge into one global component. This is not a search
restricted to individual Gomory-Hu tree cuts.
4. For detached components retain total size n, total inbound mass w, and the
sum q of size squared (uniform/uniform), size times mass (mixed), or mass squared
(inbound/inbound). Let N,W be the corresponding totals over the whole graph.
The three objective numerators are N^2-(N-n)^2-q,
N*W-(N-n)*(W-w)-q, and W^2-(W-w)^2-q, respectively.
Uniform/inbound and inbound/uniform share the same numerator, with different
normalizing denominators. This explains their identical optimal partitions.
5. Dynamic programming combines every branch option at each exact spent budget.
For size squared, equal-n states need only the smallest q. For the mixed case,
compare states with equal n. After a future detached size f their difference is
(N-n-f)*delta(w)-delta(q). It is affine for 0<=f<=remaining branch size.
For mass squared the difference after future mass f is likewise affine, with
each state's contribution 2*W*w-w^2-q-2*f*w. Compare both endpoints of the
interval 0<=f<=remaining branch mass. A state strictly inferior at both endpoints
can never win under ANY common future completion. Equal endpoint pairs are
deduplicated deterministically. Otherwise keep the state. Thus pruning is a
proved dominance rule, not an approximation. The count and mass bounds may be
loose; this only retains extra states. Original graph replay verifies each result.
6. The secondary problem maximizes score/disrupted passenger-segments among
NONEMPTY cuts with <=6 routes. Dinkelbach iteration exactly maximizes
denominator*objective numerator - numerator*disrupted passengers. The penalty
is additive and the same dominance proof applies after adding it to q. Starting
at zero, each positive residual strictly improves the rational ratio. The finite
cut space ensures termination at residual zero, which certifies global ratio
optimality within the six-route cap. This is NOT an unlimited-cardinality cost
optimum or a passenger-budget optimum. All arithmetic used in optimization and
comparisons is integer or Fraction. BCw alone uses NetworkX floating distances.
Deterministic ties use fewer routes, then canonical lexicographic route tuples.
There is no polynomial-time claim: local enumeration and Pareto fronts can grow.
Explicit local-subset/state limits raise an error before any incomplete result is
reported as exact. The report records the actual exhaustive work completed.
Reference: https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/algorithms/generated/networkx.algorithms.flow.gomory_hu_tree.html

Strongest structural finding
The connected nine-airport Washington group has 30 internal routes carrying 27,447 passenger-segments but only three boundary routes carrying 183 (37 performed departures). It is cardinality-optimal at b=3 for uniform/airports, inbound/airports, and uniform/inbound.
At b=5 these three objectives prefer the connected 12-airport group obtained by adding ESD, FRD and RNT to the nine-airport group. At b=6 they add a separate singleton, rather than BFI to form the connected thirteen-airport group.
For uniform/airports, the b=6 optimum has component sizes 430,12,1 and score 11204/443; the connected thirteen-airport cut gives 11180/443, lower by 24/443. The latter disrupts only 3,713 passenger-segments, versus 28,044 for the canonical cardinality optimum.

Effect of source prior
With airport-count targets, moving from uniform to inbound-proportional sources favors isolating PGV rather than the canonical equal-count choice AXX at b=1, and PGV rather than AXX alongside the Washington group at b=4 and b=6.
Inbound/airports and uniform/inbound have identical optimal partitions because their objective numerators are identical, although their score units and normalizations differ. When both source and target use inbound traffic, the six-route optimum instead isolates COD, GCC, PGV, PUW and SHR as five singletons.

Cost versus structural importance
All four primary fixed rankings (BC, inverse-passenger BCw, weak, strong) leave the graph connected at every budget 1..6, giving zero protection for all four objectives. BC/passenger-cost isolates IL4, but does not complete further useful cuts through b=6.
The exact protection-per-passenger optimum within six routes isolates IL4 via IL4--ORD (two annual passenger-segments, two performed departures) for the first three objectives. This exposes sensitivity of a ratio objective to extremely low recorded traffic.
For inbound/inbound, the exact efficiency optimum is instead the nine-airport Washington boundary: roughly 55,068 inbound-weight units protected per 183 disrupted passenger-segments, about 300.9 units per disrupted segment. This is a weighted static graph quantity, not a count of distinct people.
Cardinality-optimal cuts are evaluated using observed passenger-segments and performed departures; these costs do not enter the primary objective. The separate efficiency solver has a six-route cap, not an unlimited passenger-budget guarantee.

Candidate paper finding
In the specified 2025 contiguous-US scheduled-service network, an exact three-route cut separates a connected nine-airport Washington group while disrupting 183 of 797,071,268 retained annual passenger-segments. It is optimal for three of four source/target objectives; the four conventional fixed rankings produce no separation through six removals. Source/target weighting and passenger disruption yield different optimal interventions. These results concern static route-network connectivity, not measured epidemic outcomes.

Main graph: k=1, giant component only, 3105 counties and 24338 undirected edges. The complete contiguous-US universe has 3109 counties; four isolated counties are excluded only from the main optimization.
Direction-specific filter: retain uv iff at least one directed estimate exceeds k times THAT direction's MOE, strictly. Weight is the sum of BOTH reported directions, including any direction that fails the filter. Missing reverse flow contributes zero. Self-flows never create edges.
County commuter mass = sum of all reported residence-origin worker estimates, including within-county workers and destinations outside the contiguous US. These masses are fixed before reliability filtering. Source weights are renormalized on the graph being scored. Targets use the same fixed masses.
Contiguous US means the 48 states plus DC; county equivalents are included. County FIPS are zero-padded five-digit strings. All source-workplace records, including rows without a US workplace FIPS, contribute to the resident total.
The objective is static: a(V)-sum p(C)*a(C), with at most b undirected relationships removed before connectivity is evaluated. This does not change the sequential production model. County-weighted protection is a graph exposure proxy, not an epidemiological estimate of protected people.
BC and inverse-flow BCw are computed once on the original main graph, normalized=False and multiplied by 2 for ordered pairs. Scores are NetworkX floating-point outputs; rank positions break ties by canonical FIPS pairs. Weak/strong use increasing/decreasing total flow. No source information enters these rankings.
EXHAUSTIVENESS
The existing air application partition routine is reused read-only: on a temporary graph copy, resident mass is supplied under its inbound key and commuter flow under its passengers key. Those adapter keys never reinterpret or modify any existing air results.
A unit-capacity Gomory-Hu tree contracts pairs whose minimum cut exceeds 4. Such vertices cannot be separated by any feasible cut, even if a contracted block is not induced-connected. Every feasible partition is therefore a partition of whole blocks.
Restore every removed edge internal to a resulting component. The remaining cut is exactly its partition boundary; parallel original edges between two blocks must all be removed or need not be removed. Enumerate all local bundle subsets of cardinality at most 4.
Remove the largest block from the quotient. The remaining connected branches interact only through this block. Every feasible global partition restricts to one local partition per branch. Conversely each combination of local options with total boundary cost <=4 gives a feasible partition. The new exhaustive recursion visits all such combinations, without dominance pruning, and compares integer objective numerators. It retains every tied optimal partition boundary.
Returned co-optima are all distinct optimal component partitions and their minimal boundary edge sets, not redundant extra removals inside components. Each component partition has exactly one such boundary. Equal scores prefer fewer cuts then canonical FIPS order for the representative. A hard state limit raises an error rather than reporting an approximate optimum.

MAIN FINDINGS
Every objective/budget case has one optimal component partition. At b=1 all four objectives isolate Big Bend via Brewster-Pecos. Its ordinary BC rank is 179 and inverse-flow BCw rank is 1069. Rank-1 ordinary BC instead selects Cook County, IL--Douglas County, NE; this edge is not a bridge.
At b=2 all four objectives isolate Alamosa, Conejos, Costilla, Mineral, Rio Grande and Saguache Counties, Colorado. Their 19095 resident-worker mass exceeds Big Bend's 8039. The coordinated two-edge boundary is Chaffee--Saguache (74) and Costilla--Taos (26), totaling 100 workers; neither edge alone is a bridge.
For uniform/counties, commuters/counties and uniform/commuters, b=3 combines the Colorado group and Big Bend; b=4 additionally separates Edwards and Real Counties, Texas, via Real--Uvalde (203). The latter pair has resident-worker mass 2147.
For commuters/commuters, b=3 instead isolates Josephine County, Oregon (32206 resident workers), and b=4 combines that singleton with Big Bend. The cross-state endpoints of its boundary do not make Josephine a multi-county region.
All four fixed rankings leave the main graph connected for b=1,2,3,4, so all their protection scores and exact ratios are zero. The Colorado optimum requires a coordinated cut: its two edges have ordinary BC ranks 110 and 280, and weighted-BC ranks 708 and 6978. Source and target weighting changes which feasible partition is most valuable.

INTERPRETATION AND LIMITS
All four objectives select Brewster-Pecos at b=1. The exact regional comparisons and all co-optima above determine the larger-budget results; a cardinality-optimal representative need not minimize disruption among ties.
Reliability filtering changes the topology substantially. A retained bridge is a bridge of the filtered aggregate graph, not proof that all real travel or infection routes run through that county pair. The threshold is a user-specified estimate/MOE rule, not a multiple-testing procedure.
The four pre-existing isolated counties create positive baseline protection if included; the main giant-component scores intentionally exclude that effect. Source priors and target masses are graph weights, with no stochastic or temporal mobility model.

reports.competitiontheory:
EXACT THEORY OF THE COMPETING BOTTLENECK CONSTRUCTION

Assumptions and notation
Let k>=1, k<h<=min(a,m), k<=r, and assume r-1>k, a-1>k,
m-1>k. Labels within each block are indexed from 1 in this discussion.
R_i A_i, i<=k, are the candidate edges; A_j B_j, j<=h, are the
gateway edges. The code uses consecutive zero-based labels instead.
BC is the unnormalized ordered-pair edge betweenness. Write beta=BC/2
while counting unordered source-target pairs, and multiply by 2 at the end.

Unique minimum cut and optimal static partition
For a clique of size s, a nontrivial partition with t vertices on one side
has t(s-t)>=s-1 crossing edges. Thus deleting at most k edges cannot
disconnect any of the three cliques. At least one A-B edge survives,
because h>k, so A and B remain in the same connected component. If even
one R-A edge survives, the whole graph remains connected. Consequently
the only disconnecting edge set of size at most k is precisely all k
candidate edges. This proves edge connectivity k and uniqueness of the
minimum edge-cut set (the two sides of its partition are unordered).
For a uniform source and unit targets, the component identity stated as
Proposition 5.1 gives n-sum_C |C|^2/n. Every other allowed cut gives zero,
whereas the candidate cut gives 2r(a+m)/(r+a+m)>0. Hence its cut set and
partition {R,A union B} are uniquely optimal for budget k.

Shortest-path counting
A shortest path never detours through a third clique to travel within
one clique. Paths between R and A do not use B; paths between A and B do
not use R. A shortest R-B path crosses each matching exactly once.
For two cliques joined by t matching edges, between matched endpoints
with different indices there are two shortest paths; between an unmatched
endpoint and a matched endpoint there is one; between two unmatched
endpoints there are t. The matching edges share all cross-block pairs
symmetrically. It follows that each R-A edge receives ra/k from R-A
pairs, and each A-B edge receives am/h from A-B pairs.

The additional R-B paths are as follows. In this table i<=k; j denotes
the target index in B; x>k denotes an unmatched vertex of R.
Source/target                 Length  Count  Gateway shares
R_i,B_i                        2       1    gateway i: 1
R_i,B_j, j<=k, j!=i             3       3    gateway i: 1/3; gateway j: 2/3
R_i,B_j, k<j<=h                3       2    gateways i and j: 1/2 each
R_i,B_j, j>h                   3       1    gateway i: 1
R_x,B_j, j<=k                  3       1    gateway j: 1
R_x,B_j, k<j<=h                4      2k    gateway j: 1/2; each shared gateway: 1/(2k)
R_x,B_j, j>h                   4       k    each shared gateway: 1/k

For example, the three paths in the second row are
R_i A_i B_i B_j, R_i A_i A_j B_j, and R_i R_j A_j B_j.
The 2k paths in the sixth row are, for each i<=k,
R_x R_i A_i B_i B_j and R_x R_i A_i A_j B_j.
These exhaust the possible shortest routes; any other route adds a step.

All k candidate edges are symmetric, so they divide the rm R-B pairs
equally. For a fixed shared gateway A_i B_i with i<=k, the first k sources
contribute k+(h-k)/2+(m-h)=(2m+k-h)/2. The r-k remaining sources contribute
(r-k)[1+(h-k)/(2k)+(m-h)/k]=(r-k)(2m+k-h)/(2k).
The total is r(2m+k-h)/(2k). For an unshared gateway A_j B_j, k<j<=h,
only pairs targeting B_j contribute; each of the r sources contributes
1/2. Thus its R-B contribution is r/2.

The three cross-block formulas are therefore
C = BC(R_i A_i) = 2r(a+m)/k,
S = BC(A_i B_i), i<=k = 2am/h + r(2m+k-h)/k,
T = BC(A_j B_j), k<j<=h = 2am/h + r.
In particular S-T=r(2m-h)/k>0. There are exactly k edges of type S.

Internal edge classes and their pair contributions
In R, s means a matched vertex and u means an unmatched vertex.
In A and B, s means index <=k, t means k<index<=h, and u means index>h.
All vertices with the same type are interchangeable under simultaneous
permutations of matched indices. Classes with too few endpoints are absent.
The following table gives UNORDERED contributions to a single edge.
The 'within' column is its own endpoint pair in a clique. Zero entries
mean no shortest paths of that vertex-pair type use the edge.

Edge class      within       R-A             A-B             R-B
candidate       0            ra/k            0               rm/k
shared gateway  0            0               am/h            r(2m+k-h)/(2k)
other gateway   0            0               am/h            r/2
Rss             1            1               0               2/3
Rsu             1            a/k             0               m/k
Ruu             1            0               0               0
Ass             1            1               1               2/3
Ast             1            r/k             1               r/(2k)
Asu             1            r/k             m/h             0
Att             1            0               1               0
Atu             1            0               m/h             0
Auu             1            0               0               0
Bss             1            0               1               2/3
Bst             1            0               1               r/(2k)
Bsu             1            0               a/h             r/k
Btt             1            0               1               0
Btu             1            0               a/h             0
Buu             1            0               0               0

To justify the internal entries, a within-clique edge can occur on a
cross-block shortest path only as the first, last, or intervening clique
step. The two-clique path counts above give contribution 1 for two matched
endpoints, and opposite-clique-size/matching-size for one unmatched endpoint.
For R-B pairs the seven-row table supplies all remaining entries. For
example an Ast or Bst edge receives 1/2 from its matched R source and
(r-k)/(2k) from unmatched R sources, totaling r/(2k). An Rss, Ass, or Bss
edge receives 1/3 from each of the two oppositely indexed pairs, totaling
2/3. An Rsu edge receives 1+(m-k)/k=m/k from R-B pairs; a Bsu edge receives
1+(r-k)/k=r/k. All other R-B entries are zero. Multiplying each row sum
by 2 gives the ordered-pair formula for that internal edge class.

Why no internal edge can interfere with the boundary comparison
Put c=C/2=r(a+m)/k. Half the BC of any internal edge is at most
M=max{11/3, 1+(a+m)/k, 2+3r/(2k), 1+r/k+m/h, 1+r/k+a/h}.
Every term is strictly smaller than c under the stated assumptions:
c>6>11/3; c-[1+(a+m)/k]=(r-1)(a+m)/k-1>0;
c-[2+3r/(2k)]=(r/k)(a+m-3/2)-2>0.
Since h>k,
c-[1+r/k+m/h]>[r(a-1)+(r-1)m-k]/k>0,
and the final term follows by interchanging a and m.
Thus every internal edge has BC<C; S>T; and the only possible competitors
to the k candidate edges are the k shared gateways.

Candidate proposition: exact BC failure threshold
For G(r,a,m;k,h) satisfying the assumptions, let canonical tie breaking
order R labels before A labels before B labels. The candidate boundary
is the unique optimal static budget-k cut and has value 2r(a+m)/(r+a+m).
Define Delta=2kam-rh(2a+h-k). If Delta>0, the top k individual BC edges
are exactly the shared gateways A_i B_i, i<=k. Removing them leaves the
graph connected and gives zero protection. If Delta<0, the top k edges
are exactly the candidate boundary and BC attains the optimum. If Delta=0,
those two classes tie, and canonical lexicographic ordering selects the
candidate boundary. Thus under exact-score canonical ties, BC fails iff
                         2kam > rh(2a+h-k).
Proof: the path counts give S-C=Delta/(kh). There are k shared gateways,
all unshared gateways have smaller BC than S, and every internal edge
has BC<C. These comparisons prove the ranking claims; the minimum-cut
argument proves the protection claims. At equality, every candidate edge
has its first endpoint in R and precedes every gateway edge lexicographically.
Floating-point implementations need not preserve an exact tie; the saved
70 graphs are checked for Delta=0 separately below.

Family simplifications
Both families have r=3k, a=60-m. Failure is equivalent to
              2m(60-m) > 3h(120-2m+h-k).
Family A (r=6,k=2): 2m(60-m) > 3h(118-2m+h).
Family B (r=9,k=3): 2m(60-m) > 3h(117-2m+h).
Equivalently h is strictly below the positive root
H=[-(2a-k)+sqrt((2a-k)^2+8kam/r)]/2.
The right-hand side rh(2a+h-k) is strictly increasing for h>0 here.
Threshold equality counts as success under exact canonical tie breaking.
These inequalities come from shortest-path enumeration, not a fitted proxy.

VERIFICATION AGAINST THE EXISTING 70 GRAPHS
Only competition.build and the saved competition.csv are used; no optimizer or earlier sweep is rerun.
An independent verifier enumerates all shortest paths from BFS predecessor DAGs and accumulates
Fraction shares separately for within-block, R-A, A-B, and R-B pairs. All four columns are checked,
for every edge, against the derived table. This is a rational path count, not a numerical fit.

Expected students uses class-size prior. Mean ratio is prior-weighted conditional on OPT>0; worst ratio also excludes OPT0.

I. INTERPRETATION
An illustrative class-separation intervention suppresses mixing between the two named classes, such as shared activities or schedule overlap.
Static bridges separate entire student-weighted components; pairs can be valuable jointly even when neither edge is a bridge.
Sequential CSV traces identify frontier/proactive timing and final safe endpoints for every removed edge, including all optimal source solutions.
Contact loss is cumulative observed cross-class pair-contact seconds on the removed ties; not money, elapsed closure time, or a feasibility estimate.
Static optimization chooses one source-blind cut set with budget1 or2. Sequential optimization observes the source and has no global removal budget.
Their expectations therefore compare different information and resource constraints, not timing alone.
No public-health recommendation is made.

K. LIMITATIONS AND MODELING CONCERNS
Metadata conflict: student28 is2BIO2 in metadata but2BIO1 in1321 contact rows. All results use metadata; embedded-label alternatives change durations.
Metadata includes students2 and478 with no contact rows. These remain in class weights; this differs from the327-node individual contact graph.
A class vertex is an indivisible infection unit: any infection in a class exposes its whole student weight under this model.
Retaining one observed cross-class contact makes deterministic transmission possible across the whole class pair.
The complete week graph has sequential OPT0 for every source, and static budgets1/2 also save0.
Thresholding removes weaker observed routes before the process. Benefits at higher theta depend on this changed baseline, not just on the scored interventions.
Class graph strengths are pair-contact seconds, without class-size normalization. Strength affects rankings, not transmission speed.
Controlled infection rounds are not calibrated to20-second sensor intervals. Aggregation discards chronological contact order.
Daily graphs are robustness descriptions of the aggregation; not a temporal transmission model.
Connected-baseline results must not be extrapolated to disconnected levels or interpreted as causal intervention effects.
No manuscript edit, production semantic change, or Git use.

CO-OPTIMALITY AND COUNTING CONVENTIONS
Budget means at most b, including unused slots. A meaningful cut is the complete
boundary D(P) of a final component partition P. The existing contracted catalog
enumerates every attainable partition through b=4, but not every redundant edge
removal that leaves the same partition. We list every co-optimal partition and its
unique boundary cut, and separately count ALL co-optimal original edge subsets.

For each attainable partition P and exact cardinality k, put q=|D(P)|. There are
binom(m-q,k-q) size-k edge sets containing D(P). Every such set yields exactly one
attainable refinement R of P. Therefore, working from finer to coarser partitions,
N_k(P)=binom(m-q,k-q)-sum_{R strictly refining P} N_k(R), with zero when k<q.
Summing N_k(P) over optimal P and k<=b gives the exact number of optimal edge sets,
including redundant removals. Counts over ALL partitions sum to binom(m,k), which
is checked for every graph and k. Integer arithmetic is used throughout.

Each reported edge-set family is a lossless compact enumeration: take its boundary
D(P), add any subset R of E(G)\D(P) of size <= b-|D(P)|, and exclude any R containing
a listed forbidden refinement set. A forbidden set is D(Q)\D(P) for a feasible
strict refinement Q; supersets of another forbidden set are omitted. These families
are disjoint because their final partitions differ. We explicitly list all edge
sets only when there are <=100 and at most 10000 supersets need checking. Otherwise
the exact count and compact family replace a potentially enormous literal list.

Structurally unique means one labelled component partition, ignoring redundant
removals. Role-profile uniqueness is reported separately and ignores person IDs.
The giant is the unique largest component in these data. A full partition is its
listed non-giant components plus their complement in the graph's vertex roster.
The CSV also lists all giant IDs explicitly. A component is safe iff the source is
outside it: safe probability=1-p(C), expected target contribution=a(C)(1-p(C)).
No component is unconditionally 'safe' unless its source probability is zero.
The claim about multi-patient groups refers to NON-GIANT components; a giant with
many patients can also be protected when the source falls in an isolated HCW.
All ranks are 1-based positions in the existing fixed canonical ranking; equal
scores/durations use numeric lexicographic edge order. Duration ranks are given
both weakest-first and strongest-first. Bridge status is on the uncut baseline.

Candidate paper findings
- In these four selected hospital graphs and budgets1-4, exactly three graph/prior/target/budget cases have an optimal non-giant group larger than one: full60 at b=4 with uniform/all, HCW/all or HCW/PAT; the group is two administrators.
- No co-optimal non-giant component contains two patients. Patient separations in these optima are individual singleton components, not multi-patient groups.
- More budget can change the set of optimal partitions without changing the optimum value: Tuesday uniform/all has one optimal partition at b=2,3 and seven at b=4.
- Source priors and target populations change optimal identities. Isolating HCWs can protect patients in the large remaining component when the source lies among those isolated HCWs.
- The night uniform/all optimum over b=1..4 is explained by independent leaf separations, with exact score b*(105-b)/53; this is nearly linear but has decreasing increments.
- Fixed edge rankings can fail to complete a coordinated small boundary cut. In full60 at b=4 all four heuristics leave the graph connected despite a positive exact optimum for every tested objective.
- These are properties of the specified static thresholded aggregates, not estimates of clinical intervention effectiveness.

Each row is one 20-second interval [t-20,t]; times are relative to 2010-12-06 13:00 Europe/Paris.
The full aggregate uses all recorded bins (roughly four days spanning five calendar dates).
Day/night selection uses the recorded interval ENDPOINT. Night: endpoint hour>=20 or <7.

Vertices are all people active in the selected period BEFORE duration thresholding; isolates are retained.
Retain an edge iff duration>=threshold; duration=20 times its number of selected bins.
HCW means NUR, MED or ADM. Priors are uniform on the selected source population within each graph.
Target weights are 1 for all people, or 1 only for PAT. Zero target weights are allowed.
STATIC model: choose one fixed removal set of cardinality AT MOST b before infection from the unknown source.
No mandatory spread, sequential intervention, or recomputed centrality is involved in this application.
Score = a(V)-sum_C p(C)a(C). Values and comparisons use exact rational arithmetic.
All six combinations of three source priors and two target objectives are included.
BC uses ordinary unweighted paths; BCw uses length 1/duration. Both use unnormalized ordered-pair values (2 times NetworkX).
Heuristics remove their initial top b canonical edges. Ties use canonical numeric endpoint order.
OPT ties prefer fewer cuts, then lexicographic cuts. Ratios are NA when OPT=0.
Counts, optimal partitions and cuts were replayed on the original person-level graphs.
All 16 supplied budget-2 scores reproduced exactly.

EXACTNESS CERTIFICATE
Give every original edge capacity 1, irrespective of contact duration. A Gomory-Hu
tree represents each pairwise minimum edge cut by the minimum tree-edge weight on
its path. Delete tree edges of weight <= B. Each remaining tree component is an
atom: any two of its vertices require more than B original edges to separate.
Consequently every component of G-F, for |F|<=B, is a union of entire atoms.

Given any feasible F, restore every removed edge whose endpoints lie in the same
component of G-F. This preserves the component partition and hence the objective,
and never increases the number of removals. The remaining cuts are exactly all
original edges crossing that partition. No edge internal to an atom is cut. Between
any two atoms either all original edges are cut, or none need be cut: a surviving
edge joins those atoms in one component. Thus group these parallel original edges
into bundles, whose cardinality is their removal cost, and exhaustively enumerate
bundle subsets of total cost <= B, including the empty subset.

Every feasible component partition has a representative in this enumeration. For
each enumerated subset, quotient components give the original components: atoms
remain connected in the surviving original graph by their >B cut connectivity,
even if an atom's induced subgraph is disconnected. Remove redundant internal
bundles, retain the unique boundary cut of each partition, and score that partition.
This also supplies every optimum for b=0,...,B by restricting to boundary cost<=b.
All objective comparisons use exact Fraction arithmetic. Ties prefer fewer cuts,
then lexicographically smallest canonical edge tuples. This does not claim to list
all optimal removal sets with redundant edges.

There are n-c max-flow computations for c original components. Enumeration visits
each bundle subset with total cost<=B, rather than every original edge subset.
This is an exhaustive reduction, not a polynomial-time guarantee for arbitrary
graphs: when atoms are singletons and all bundles have size 1, the reduction may
give no benefit. No approximation, timeout incumbent, or heuristic pruning is used.
Gomory-Hu reference: https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/algorithms/generated/networkx.algorithms.flow.gomory_hu_tree.html

OBJECTIVES AND INTERPRETATION
A: uniform county source, county targets; Q_A=(n*n-sum size(C)^2)/n, measured in expected counties.
B: uniform county source, population targets; Q_B=(n*W-sum size(C)*population(C))/n, measured in expected people.
C (primary): population-proportional county source, population targets; Q_C=(W*W-sum population(C)^2)/W, measured in expected people.
For A interventions the separately reported expected population is Q_B, because A uses a uniform county source. For B and C expected population equals the objective.
fractionW uses that expected population divided by W. Ratios to OPT always compare the same objective and budget.
A detached/non-giant component is not guaranteed safe: it is protected only if the random source lies in another component.
For each component, the CSV records size, census population, source probability and population*(1-source probability), including the giant component.
Thus expected protected population can exceed the detached population: a source in a detached region protects the large remainder.
Infeasible fixed cuts retain their actual partition score for transparency, are explicitly marked infeasible, and have no achieved/OPT ratio.

Existing commuting.catalog and commuting.exact are reused. A temporary graph copy maps population to resident, which the existing catalog maps to its inbound mass key. Original commuter attributes and graph data are not changed.
Unit-capacity Gomory-Hu contraction at budget 2 groups vertices whose pairwise edge min-cut exceeds 2; no feasible removal can split such a block.
Every final partition uses whole blocks. Restoring removed edges inside a final component preserves all three objectives, so only minimal partition boundaries need be enumerated.
The quotient is split into branches around its largest block. The existing local search enumerates all bundle subsets of cost <=2; the existing global search enumerates all combinations of branch partitions of total cost <=2.
All comparisons use integer numerators uu, mixed, pp, divided exactly by n,n,W. No population-based pruning is introduced.
All tied optimal minimal boundaries are retained. Representative ties prefer fewer removed edges, then canonical lexicographic FIPS edge tuples.

BASELINES
Initial BC and recomputed BC interventions are read from unchanged caches and their partitions replayed on the reconstructed graph. No centralities or earlier sweeps are rerun.
Cached BC uses unnormalized ordinary NetworkX values times 2 for ordered pairs and canonical edge ties. Stored BC tie counts are reused; unavailable counts remain null.
Objective Greedy is run separately for A, B and C. It selects the exact maximum marginal gain, canonical lexicographic ties, including zero-gain choices if necessary.
Only a current bridge has nonzero one-step gain. For a split into sides with sizes x,y and populations p,q, marginal gains are 2xy/n, (xq+yp)/n, and 2pq/W for A,B,C.
Bridge status, DFS subtree sizes and population sums evaluate these exact gains on each current graph. Brute-force small tests independently check every edge gain.

5. This is deterministic reachability protection in a static county graph, not an estimate of actual infections, hospitalizations, or travel risk.
Uniform county sources give a small county the same source probability as a large one. Population-proportional sources correspond to selecting a resident uniformly and locating the source in that resident's county, an assumption rather than an estimated introduction-risk model.
Each infected county is treated as exposing all its residents; no within-county dynamics, transmission probabilities, timing or heterogeneity is represented.
An edge deletion suppresses an entire aggregated commuting relationship in both directions. Budgets count relationships, not commuters, closure feasibility or economic disruption.
The graph uses 2016-2020 ACS estimates filtered by their reported MOEs; population is a 2020 Census count. Reliability filtering and giant-component restriction condition every result.
These findings concern only the evaluated graph, population vintage and budgets. They are not causal public-health forecasts or a recommendation to close the named links.

INDEPENDENT RANDOM-GRAPH SEQUENTIAL BENCHMARK
Master seed 20261115; Python 3.13.12; NetworkX 3.7.
Production safezones.exact, safezones.centralities and safezones.simulate are called without modification.
A0={source}; mandatory first spread on the original graph; then at most one permanent removal or wait before each simultaneous spread.
Infection is permanent; stop at no new infection; no global deletion budget. Objective: final uninfected vertex count.
Exact search memoizes infected vertices and surviving edges; waiting and susceptible-susceptible actions are allowed.
Redundant infected-infected removals are omitted by the production exact solver.
Weak/strong use smallest/largest strength. BC and BCw scores are computed on the original graph only.
BCw distances are inverse strength. Production scores are unnormalized unordered NetworkX BC (half the paper ordered-pair value).
All ranking and tie conventions are used unchanged. Source-aware BC uses its production 1e-12 tolerance on stored BC scores.
Threshold BC considers only current infected-susceptible edges; other policies may make proactive cuts.
Existing removals and infected-infected edges are excluded. Supplying cached centralities is checked to prevent recomputation.
The exact solver returns cut order without wait slots. Stored exactreplay is a separately verified legal earliest-cut realization, not a transcript of internal search.
Moving unrestricted cuts earlier cannot speed infection; the independent replay is required to attain the returned exact value.

SAMPLING AND REPRODUCIBILITY
Graph attempts use nx.gnp_random_graph or nx.stochastic_block_model. No disconnected graph is repaired or reduced to a giant component.
Graphs are generated from independent domain-separated RNG seeds. Accepted graphs are conditioned on connectedness and global nonisomorphism.
Duplicate screening ignores labels and SBM block membership; connected isomorphic repeats are rejected, including across configurations with the same n.
Therefore the accepted set is not an IID sample from the unconditioned ER/SBM distributions. It is a reproducible conditioned, distinct-topology sample.
Processing order is A, B, C, D; cross-configuration duplicate rejection is documented below.
Seed derivation: first 8 SHA256 bytes, big-endian, of master|domain|configuration|index.
Topology domain uses attempt numbers starting at 1; sources domain uses accepted index 0..9; strength domain additionally appends realization 0 or 1.
Three source vertices are sampled uniformly without replacement using a separate RNG, then sorted for evaluation.
Two independently seeded Uniform(1,10) strength assignments use canonical edge order. Each draw is shared by all three sources and all six policies.
Exact optimization runs once per tested topology/source; its result is reused across both strength draws.
Repeated source/strength evaluations are not counted as independent graph topologies.
All 40 topology choices and sources are generated before looking at exact-solver runtime or policy performance.

reports.transmission:
STOCHASTIC TRANSMISSION ROBUSTNESS
Independent bond percolation on original undirected edges. Interventions are fixed BEFORE drawing any active edges.
Each realization integrates over the source prior exactly: Q=a(V)-sum p(C)a(C). Source trials are not sampled separately.
Gain means E[Q(F)]-E[Q(empty)], not total expected protection. Priors and target weights stay fixed across realizations.
Air: 443 airports, 7160 routes, tau=1; uniform source, unit targets. Only the cached fixed interventions are compared.
A deterministic optimal cut need not be stochastically optimal; no stochastic global optimality claim is made for air.
School: 9 classes, 12 edges with duration >=5300 seconds, 329 metadata students including two without contact rows.
School target weights are class population under BOTH source priors.
No original code, result, figure or manuscript file is modified. No BC ranking or measured static optimization is rerun.

METHOD AND UNCERTAINTY
Python 3.13.12, NetworkX 3.7; random.Random seed=20261115.
Canonical sorted original edges determine RNG order. For each stochastic q the same seed is reset, coupling q levels as well as interventions.
Within a trial every intervention uses the identical original-edge activity vector. Active cut edges are then suppressed.
Union-find first merges active edges outside the union of all intervention sets; each intervention gets a copy and adds its surviving active special edges.
This reuse is exact because all interventions share those common active edges. Vertices, including isolates, are never dropped.
Air q<1 starts with 1000 trials. Requested gain CIs are pointwise paired normal 95% intervals: mean +/- 1.959964 SE.
They are Monte Carlo approximations, not exact finite-sample guarantees; intervals are not clipped at zero.
For comparison decisions, 97.5%-per-look paired normal intervals allow at most two looks (a union-bound approximate 95% guarantee per comparison).
There is no simultaneous error guarantee across all q values or all intervention comparisons.
Extend a q batch to 3000 coupled trials only if a full-versus-baseline/partial comparison straddles zero with decision halfwidth >0.10 airport.
After an extension the first 1000 trials are retained and 2000 new trials continue the same RNG stream.
A comparison is unresolved unless its decision interval excludes zero; zero observed variance does not prove zero true stochastic benefit.
Ratios are ratios of estimated incremental gains, not mean trial ratios and not achieved-to-stochastic-OPT ratios.
At q=1 the single full-edge configuration is evaluated exactly; its degenerate intervals are deterministic identities.
School enumerates all 4096 ORIGINAL edge configurations, including edges later removed. Probabilities are q^k(1-q)^(12-k).
Integer coefficient sums by active-edge count and Fraction arithmetic give exact expectations for every tested rational q.
All school best/runner-up differences are exact. No school Monte Carlo confidence intervals are used.
Air runtimes are shared per-q coupled batches, not additive per-intervention timings.
School enumeration/coefficient construction: 0.023224s.

VALIDATION
PASS all source priors normalize exactly; all five cached deterministic school prior optima replayed
PASS all 4096 school component configurations and both weighted objectives match independent NetworkX replay
PASS shared-union-find air realizations match independent replay for all 11 interventions in 10 configurations
PASS q=0 gives zero intervention benefit, with nonzero baseline protection; q=1 matches every cached air baseline and school intervention
PASS fixed interventions, deterministic replay, nonnegative paired gains and confidence-interval arithmetic
PASS all input-file hashes and graph topologies unchanged after the full experiment
Air q=0: total expected protection 442, intervention gain 0 for every cut.
School q=0 class-uniform: expected protection 2632/9 (292.444444444); intervention gains all 0.
School q=0 population: expected protection 13722/47 (291.957446809); intervention gains all 0.

MODEL AND EXACTNESS
Select the largest undirected component once; keep that entire vertex set after all removals. All active markets belong to the giant in both periods, so no active vertices are excluded.
Uniform source over giant vertices; unit target per market. Q(F)=(n^2-sum(component sizes squared))/n. No cuts gives Q=0. Static cuts precede transmission; no sequential simulator is used.
A detached component is protected when the source lies elsewhere; it is not guaranteed safe for every source. Q is expected protected markets, not detached-region size.
Reuse air.partitions and air.optimize(mode=uu). An adapter sets inbound=1 and passengers=1 solely for the existing solver fields; neither represents livestock population or scaled shipment volume.
Completeness: capacity-one Gomory-Hu contraction merges vertices inseparable by <=b edges. Every feasible final component is a union of atoms.
Restoring removals internal to final components preserves Q and lowers cost. Thus every relevant cut removes whole inter-atom bundles.
The solver exhaustively enumerates local bundle subsets within budget in every branch around the largest atom, then combines branch partitions by its exact DP. All root components merge; detached sizes and their squared-size sum determine Q.
For uniform/unit targets, DP dominance preserves every optimum because equal detached total size has the same final root size and a smaller squared-size sum is never worse. This is not a search over single Gomory-Hu edges.
Best single-region comparison: a two-component global partition has one detached component in one quotient branch. Enumerating completed local options with exactly one detached component gives the exact best two-component value under the same budget.
Feasibility gate: reconstruct both graphs and solve budget 1 first, capped at min(20,45) seconds each. Continue only if both connected giants have at least 3 vertices and both pilot optima are verified.
Budgets 2 and 3 each have a 45-second wall cap and 200000 local-enumeration/DP-combination limits. No failed search supplies an OPT or approximation ratio.
BC policy code is imported from research/baselines/baseline.py. Ordered-pair BC=2*NetworkX normalized=False; canonical string ID pairs break equal computed scores lexicographically.
Initial BC ranks once; recomputed BC ranks after each previous deletion. Each BC step has a 20-second cap and each graph a 60-second cumulative recomputed cap.
Per-step BC/greedy selection times and cumulative selection times are recorded; replay and diagnostic time is included only in total pilot runtime. The first BC computation is shared by initial and recomputed policies.
Objective Greedy uses exact integer marginal numerators: a bridge splitting a current component into x and y gives 2xy/n; all non-bridges give zero. Zero-gain ties are recorded and resolved lexicographically.

LIMITATIONS
The undirected projection introduces reverse traversals not supported by recorded shipments and has much greater reachability. Directed no-cut isolation is not an intervention effect.
Static aggregation also allows paths whose shipment ordering is impossible in time; combining 2013-2017 is not an observed simultaneous network.
Survey coverage is selected, concentrated on Burkina Faso-linked corridors, changes across years, and omits incomplete or unmapped movements. The article does not claim a complete West African trade census.
Market names and countries identify recorded locations, not verified geographic compactness, common administration, or feasible closure plans. The node supplement supplies no coordinates.
Scaled boundary sums are descriptive only. No exact animal counts, disease probabilities, costs, welfare losses, or actual containment benefits are inferred.
Only one deterministic exact representative is reported per budget. No claim of unique optimum or exhaustive co-optimal enumeration is made.

1. Coordinated-cut advantage: yes in both observed periods at b=3. The three removed relationships are Fada N'Gourma--Kouremale, Bobo-Dioulasso--Kouremale and Ouagadougou--Kouremale. Each edge alone is non-separating. Initial and recomputed BC achieve zero through b=3.
2. Mechanism: a multi-link gateway feeds a downstream branching market region. All three boundary links terminate at Kouremale, and the recorded movement direction on each is Burkina Faso to Mali. This resembles the existing coordinated-boundary mechanism, not a demonstrated new universal graph mechanism.
The additional contrast is between fragmentation and regional isolation: b=2 optimally separates two smaller branch regions, whereas b=3 replaces those cuts with the entire three-link gateway. Objective Greedy commits to immediate bridge gains and cannot replace its earlier choices.
3. Interpretation: the separated connected region spans identified markets in Mali and Guinea. Names/countries are supplied, but geographic compactness and operational feasibility are not established by the CSVs.
4. Period comparison: the representative b=3 boundary is identical across both periods. The full-period region adds Diankana (n185, Guinea) to the 10-market 2017 region. The same two bridge cuts are selected at b=2. These periods overlap and differ in survey coverage; this is consistency under aggregation, not an independent replication.
5. Direction: only about one tenth of distinct ordered pairs are reachable in the directed networks. Undirected projection therefore makes a major interpretive change. The recorded b=3 boundaries are one-way inputs; directed no-cut protection is already large. Direction-aware intervention analysis is needed before making disease-control claims.
6. Sparsity: both evaluated networks are connected, so baseline fragmentation is not the explanation. There are many bridges and leaves, but the b=1 optimum already detaches 4 or 5 markets, b=2 detaches two multi-market components, and b=3 detaches 10 or 11. The exact results are not merely singleton peeling.
Greedy zero-gain ties: none in these measured runs. Its third choice has many tied POSITIVE gains: 2017=104, 2013-2017=129.
BC zero values are verified connected post-cut graphs, not failed computations. High-BC selections do not complete a separating boundary within the tested budget.
Recommendation: EXPAND PILOT. The undirected result is reproducible and interpretable, but it largely repeats a coordinated-cut mechanism while direction and incomplete survey coverage are major limitations. Next assess directed and temporally feasible containment before deciding on a fifth application.

SAN LUIS VALLEY GENERALITY PILOT

Scope: deterministic synthetic topology counterfactuals, not measured commuting changes, transport plans or geographic conclusions.
Baseline: kappa=1, strict direction-specific flow>MOE filter; aggregate both directed flows; select original largest component once. 3105 vertices, 24338 edges. No vertices are dropped or giant reselected after perturbation.
R: [{"fips": "08003", "name": "Alamosa County"}, {"fips": "08021", "name": "Conejos County"}, {"fips": "08023", "name": "Costilla County"}, {"fips": "08079", "name": "Mineral County"}, {"fips": "08105", "name": "Rio Grande County"}, {"fips": "08109", "name": "Saguache County"}]
Original R: 6 counties, 8 internal edges, density=8/15, boundary=(('08015', '08109'), ('08023', '35055')). R and its complement are connected.
All variants keep the outside induced graph identical. Both R and its complement remain connected, and so does the full graph.
Objective: uniform source over the same 3105 vertices, unit target, static fixed cuts; score=N-sum(size squared)/N. No changes to sequential semantics. Fractions are authoritative; expected protection is not the deterministic size of the detached region.
Candidate R cut: 37188/3105=12396/1035 when feasible. Infeasible cuts have the literal infeasible score, no decimal, and no BC/OPT substitution.
BC: 2*NetworkX edge_betweenness_centrality(normalized=False), exactly the ordinary-BC expression in commuting.rankings; canonical FIPS ties. Computed once on each variant, not after cutting. BCw/weak/strong are not calculated. Full-network centrality is used; high-BC edges are not assumed to bound a coherent outside region.
Solver: existing air.partitions plus air.optimize(uu), also used by the application sweeps and Washington pilot. Temporary inbound/passengers adapter values are 1; no real flow or county metadata are changed. No invented traffic weights are assigned to synthetic links.
Completeness: unit-capacity Gomory-Hu contraction keeps every <=b partition; all affordable local bundle deletions are enumerated and all global combinations are considered by the existing exact dominance DP. This is not a search restricted to R or single Gomory-Hu edges. See code/air.py:21-68.
Limits: 90 seconds per variant exact search; 200000 local visits / DP combinations. Failure leaves OPT and ratio blank, with exactstatus=unverified and a reason. Limits apply to the largest requested budget of the variant; no smaller-budget optimum is inferred from a timed-out run.
Local workbook is parsed once and the baseline graph reused in memory. The previous /private/tmp application-sweep cache was absent. No original sweep is run or written. The saved baseline exact cut/score and BC choices serve as independent regression anchors.
Internal: counts 5,6,7,8,10,12,15; seeds 0,1. Below 8 remove shuffled original edges only if connected; above 8 add shuffled missing edges. At 8, build a shuffled spanning path plus 3 shuffled absent chords to test different placements at the empirical edge count.
Boundary width: 1,3,4, seeds 0,1, plus measured width 2. At width 1 remove one original link. For larger widths add links on distinct unused regional vertices, to the two original outside anchors. Evaluate fixed b=2 and matching b=width.
Boundary placement at width 2: distinct changes regional endpoints with original outside anchors; region concentrates both links on one regional vertex; outside concentrates both on Chaffee or Taos while retaining original regional endpoints; alternate uses two shuffled one-hop neighbors of the original outside anchors and distinct shuffled regional endpoints. Seeds 0,1; R internal edges stay unchanged.
Duplicate graphs are evaluated once and retain parameter/seed aliases. A baseline control is not relabeled synthetic. All modifications and endpoints are recorded below. Two seeds are placement checks, not representative random samples.

WASHINGTON AIR-NETWORK GENERALITY PILOT

Scope: synthetic topology counterfactuals of the original tau=1 graph, not measured alternative routes.
Original graph: 443 airports, 7160 routes; R=DHB,FBS,KEH,LKE,LPS,PUL,RCE,RSJ,WSX; U=R plus BFI, ESD, FRD, RNT.
Original boundaries: |delta(R)|=3, |delta(U)|=6. No vertices are dropped and no giant is reselected.
Uniform source over all 443 airports; unit target weights; static fixed cuts; score=N-sum(component size squared)/N.
Ordinary BC is recomputed once for each counterfactual original graph, then held fixed for its cuts. air.rankings uses 2*NetworkX normalized=False and canonical lexicographic ties.
All graphs retain connected R, U, V-R and V-U. The graph is connected before intervention.
Seeds 0 and 1 shuffle canonically sorted eligible edges. Duplicate resulting graphs are evaluated once; seeds lists retain aliases.
Internal levels: 9,15,21,27,33,36 edges. Remove shuffled internal edges only if R stays connected, or add shuffled missing internal edges.
R-boundary levels: 1,2,4,5,6. Remove existing boundary edges or add absent R-to-{BFI,ESD,FRD,RNT} edges; delta(U) is unchanged.
U-boundary levels: 3,4,5,7,8,9. Modify only edges between {BFI,ESD,FRD,RNT} and V-U; delta(R) and U internal edges are unchanged.
Internal and R-boundary changes also change U internal density as a derived quantity because R is contained in U. This is not an independently fixed U-density experiment.
Budget=3 in every graph; R-boundary variants also use budget=|delta(R)|, without duplicate rows.
The full R-cut value is 7812/443 in every graph. It is an evaluated intervention, never a substitute for OPT; feasibility is recorded separately.
candidateoptimal means the R boundary ALONE attains OPT within the row budget. rinoptimal refers only to the saved representative partition, not all co-optima.
Additions are marked synthetic in memory. No passenger volume is invented. A solver/ranking copy sets all node masses and passenger fields to one; these fields are bookkeeping for the uniform/topological objective, not traffic estimates.
Exact method: unchanged air.partitions and air.optimize(uu), with unit-capacity Gomory-Hu contraction, exhaustive local partition enumeration and the existing exact dominance DP.
Completeness is the existing air.py proof: inseparable atoms preserve all <=b cuts; enumerate all affordable bundle deletions per branch; combine every feasible local partition. No restriction to a single tree edge or to R/U cuts.
Exact limits: 20 seconds per graph; 200000 local visits and 200000 DP combinations. Any limit failure leaves exact score and BC/OPT blank and records unverified plus its reason.

reports.washingtoninterpretation:
WASHINGTON PILOT: SAVED-RESULT INTERPRETATION

Scope: 34 distinct graphs and 44 graph/budget cases; 1 measured baseline and 33 synthetic counterfactuals. All 443 vertices are retained. No optimization was rerun. Saved exact results remain the source of optimality certification; all saved cut scores and partitions were independently replayed with exact rational arithmetic.

The original measured graph has OPT=7812/443=17.6343 expected protected airports at b=3, achieved by isolating R. Top-3 BC has value zero. Its R-boundary ranks are 1, 223, 210 in canonical boundary-edge order.

BC is zero in 40 of 44 cases and positive in four. It is optimal only for boundary1s1 at b=1. The two seeds at width 1 have identical OPT but different matching-budget BC performance: zero versus one in BC/OPT. With b=3, both save R but miss two additionally separable singleton airports.

Internal placement matters. At 9 internal edges, seed 0 gives OPT=8694/443 and BC/OPT=1160/1449; seed 1 gives OPT=7812/443 and BC=0. At 15 edges, the optima are 7828/443 and 7812/443, with zero BC in both. At each tested level 21, 27, 33, 36 (and the measured 30), R alone is optimal and BC is zero. This is not a universal density threshold: only two placement seeds were examined and intermediate levels were not tested.

Across families, equal total edge count and equal budget also fail to determine OPT. The complete list has eight edge-count groups, all at b=3: 7139, 7145, 7157, 7158, 7159, 7161, 7162, 7163. The first two are the seed-placement comparisons above; the other six change where edges are modified. Every case and exact value is listed in evidence.txt.

Changing R width at fixed b=3: widths 1 and 2 permit R plus extra singleton separation, improving OPT to 9542/443 and 8678/443. At matching budget, R alone is optimal at widths 1, 2, 4, 5; at width 6 the larger U cut is feasible and better (11180/443). The measured width 3 is optimal at b=3.

R alone is optimal in 28 cases, feasible but suboptimal in 10, and infeasible in 6. U is feasible and optimal in four cases; it is infeasible in the other 40. A different saved optimal cut occurs in 12 cases. These are representative solutions, not an enumeration of co-optima: uniqueness and the absence of alternative optimal cuts are not established.

The two curves at 15 internal edges nearly overlap because their exact difference is only 16/443. All non-diamond cases are synthetic, not observed alternative routes. Lines guide the eye between tested levels and are not interpolated experiments.

The pilot summary's numerical claims, 44 result lines, conditional summaries, graph modification log and four input/code hashes all agree with the saved data and reconstruction. Its fixed-budget 0/2 R-optimal counts at widths 4-6 denote infeasibility, not a zero-valued R intervention. Runtime/platform are recorded provenance and were not remeasured. No substantive numerical correction to the saved pilot report was needed.
